newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH FOOD INDUSTRY SEES FALLING PROFITABILITY.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH FOOD INDUSTRY SEES FALLING PROFITABILITY.

text.p: Profitability in the Finnish food industry has fallen clearly this year and the outlook for next year is no better, said Felix Bjorklund, chairman of the Finnish food industry federation.
In a press summary of Bjorklund's speech at the federation's autumn meeting on Monday, he was quoted as saying that prices have fallen while costs have risen.

"Consumer prices of foodstuffs have fallen about 11 percent, clearly more than authorities estimated on the basis of the fall in raw materials prices. At the same time, for instance labour costs have increased more than 10 percent," he said.

"Industry producer prices have generally fallen to an unhealthy level from the point of view of business," Bjorklund said, adding that "this kind of pricing policy cannot be pursued but the industry must also take care of its own profitability".
On the other hand, the food industry has had successes in exports this year, he said.

"The ground lost on the Russian market last year has been recovered. The development has been positive also in Sweden and other EU countries and refined foodstuffs exports will rise to about five billion markka, which is the level of the peak year 1994," he said.

The Finnish food industry exports 10 percent of its output which is high in international comparison, he said. Exports are necessary since the home market is too small to enable economies of scale, he added.

"Our industry cannot make it in the international markets for mass products. We have to focus on high quality and special products whose manufacture requires high technology and know-how. We have both," Bjorklund said.
